sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: While geographic expansion to Miami and Dallas signals continued commitment, the underlying reality is concerning: Austin fleet remains stuck at ~50 vehicles after a full year of operation, demonstrating failed scaling. Software limitations—not hardware production—remain the fundamental blocker, making city expansion premature without solving the core constraint.

positive_signals: Miami service launched with unsupervised vehicles on July 3, 2026
Dallas also added to robotaxi service coverage
negative_signals: Austin fleet still only ~50 vehicles after a year of operation
Software remains limiting factor, not vehicle production
Service expansion limited by FSD capabilities

key_metrics.actual: ~50 vehicles in Austin, new Miami/Dallas launches

keyChanges.title: Tesla robotaxi expands to Miami and Dallas on July 3
keyChanges.description: On July 3, 2026, Tesla expanded its unsupervised robotaxi service to Miami and Dallas, marking continued geographic expansion of the Cybercab platform. City officials report Tesla's Austin fleet at approximately 50 vehicles despite a year of operation. Production is ramping exponentially toward year-end per Musk, but software limitations rather than vehicle manufacturing capacity remain the primary constraint on service scaling.

keyChanges.title: Denmark becomes fourth European country to approve FSD on June 9
keyChanges.description: Denmark greenlit Tesla FSD Supervised on June 9, 2026, following Netherlands (April 10), Lithuania (May 20), and Estonia (May 29). The Dutch vehicle authority RDW granted the first European type approval, and Tesla anticipates EU-wide recognition during summer 2026 through mutual recognition, potentially extending access to Germany, France, and other major markets without repeating the full 18-month review process. Tesla now has FSD Supervised available in 12 countries globally.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Production timeline confirmed (late July/August) which is positive, but Musk's caution on 'quite slow' initial output and 10,000 unique parts tempers expectations for near-term volume.

positive_signals: Concrete production start: late July or August 2026 at Fremont
Fremont converted from Model S/X to Optimus (1M units/year capacity)
Giga Texas second-gen facility targeting 10M units/year, summer 2027 start
100+ Optimus-related job openings signal serious ramp efforts
negative_signals: Musk warned initial output will be 'quite slow'
Production rate 'literally impossible to predict' due to 10,000 unique parts
Model S/X production ended to make room (May 2026)
No commercial customer announcements or pricing confirmed

key_metrics.trajectory: On schedule but with slow initial ramp expected

keyChanges.title: Optimus production confirmed for late July/August 2026 at Fremont
keyChanges.description: During Tesla's Q1 2026 earnings call, Elon Musk confirmed that Optimus humanoid robot production will commence in late July or August 2026 at the Fremont factory. The facility, converted from Model S/X production (final vehicles produced May 2026), targets 1 million units annually. Musk cautioned that initial output will be 'quite slow' due to 10,000 unique parts across an entirely new production line. Tesla is simultaneously constructing a second-generation Optimus facility at Giga Texas targeting 10 million units per year, with production starting summer 2027.

trends: Geographic expansion prioritized over fleet scaling: Miami and Dallas robotaxi launches despite modest Austin fleet size
European FSD regulatory momentum building: 4 countries approved in 3 months (Denmark most recent on June 9)

Hardware production accelerating while software remains constraint: Cybercab production ramping but limited by FSD v15 delay to Q4 2026
